newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt cool about Arab summit proposal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt cool about Arab summit proposal.

text.p: Egypt reacted coolly on Sunday to a Palestinian suggestion to hold another Arab summit, saying regional leaders were still following through the proposals of their last meeting held in Cairo in June.
Egyptian newspapers quoted Palestinian President Yasser Arafat as saying contacts were under way to hold the summit within the next two months, with Iraq present.

But Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters on Sunday: "Holding an Arab summit requires certain measures and dynamics and we are still following up implementation of the decisions of the last summit.
"The question of holding a summit at the present time depends on what circumstances dictate and what Arab action requires," he added.
The June Arab summit was the first since 1990. Iraq was not invited because some Gulf states still refuse to sit alongside the same Iraqi government that invaded Kuwait six years ago.
The newspapers said Arafat told the Arabic-language television station ART that opposition to Iraq's presence at a summit had disappeared.
